name: Vascoril
description: Vascoril is a vascular remodeling agent designed for patients whose blood vessels have been surgically rerouted or regrown to supply chrome-adjacent tissue, SNT implants, and synthetic organ interfaces — a process that frequently produces fragile, poorly organized vascular networks prone to microhemorrhage and thrombosis. It promotes organized angiogenesis, strengthens new vessel walls, and prevents the clotting complications that cause 'chrome bleed,' the dangerous internal bleeding around augment sites.
effects: promotes organized angiogenesis around implant sites
reduces thrombosis risk in chrome-adjacent vessels
side_effects: interactions with other anticoagulants are dangerous
duration: 12 hours per dose; ongoing treatment for chronic cases
street_price: Φ18 per dose (Nightshade gray market); Φ55 prescription
cultural_context: Chrome bleed is a leading cause of death among Tier 1-2 residents who got cheap, rushed augment installations without proper vascular surgical follow-up. Vascoril is Nightshade's answer to a Lazarus prescription drug that most Shelf residents can't access or afford. It works — not as cleanly as the premium alternatives — and Nightshade distributes it through gray-market channels that reach places legitimate pharmacies don't. Its restricted status is technically about the hemorrhage risk, but practically it's about Lazarus protecting market share.
story_hooks: A rash of chrome bleed deaths on the Shelf is being traced to a bad batch of Vascoril — someone has tampered with Nightshade's supply chain
A character discovers that Vascoril's restricted status was pushed through by Lazarus lobbying, and thousands of people are dying from chrome bleed who could be saved
Nightshade's Vascoril distribution network is also being used to move something else — and a character who depends on the drug is being pressured to look the other way
